findings.explanation: The flagged line is `rows = session.execute(` in the new `batch_order_status` endpoint. The query is built with SQLAlchemy `text()` and bound `:name` parameters: `params = {f"id{i}": value for i, value in enumerate(id_list)}` and `placeholders = ", ".join(":" + key for key in params)`, then `session.execute(text("SELECT id, status FROM orders WHERE id IN (" + placeholders + ")"), params)`. The only dynamic part of the SQL string is the placeholder names (`:id0`, `:id1`, ...), which are generated from a fixed integer index (i), not from user input — so no user-controlled text is concatenated into the SQL. The actual user-supplied values (from `request.args.get("ids")`) are coerced to integers via `int(part)` (with a 400 on ValueError) and passed as bound parameters in the `params` dict, never interpolated into the query string. This matches the project's own policy (security-policy.md §5: 'All SQL statements MUST use bound parameters (SQLAlchemy text() with :name parameters...)'). The endpoint is also gated by `@require_role("manager")`. Therefore the flagged query is parameterized and not injectable — a false positive.

evidence.content: All SQL statements MUST use bound parameters (SQLAlchemy `text()` with `:name` parameters, or DB-API placeholders with a separate params argument). String interpolation, f-strings, `%` formatting, `.format()`, or string concatenation of request-derived values into SQL is forbidden (CWE-89).

findings.explanation: The new GET /batch-status endpoint fetches orders by user-supplied ids and returns their status. It is guarded only by @require_role("manager"), which authenticates and checks role but performs NO per-object ownership verification. security-policy.md §3 states: "A user may view ONLY their own orders. Every endpoint that fetches an order by its identifier MUST verify ownership with is_owner_or_admin(current_user, order.user_id) before returning data." The endpoint fetches orders by identifier (the ids query param) and returns data without calling is_owner_or_admin, so a manager can read the status of any user's orders. This is an IDOR (CWE-639). Note: the SQL itself is correctly parameterized (bound params via text() + params dict), so the SAST SQLi flag is a false positive; the real flaw is the missing authorization check. The endpoint is also not documented in api-spec.md, but the authoritative security-policy.md §3 rule is explicit and violated.

evidence.content:
## 3. Order data access rules
- A user may view ONLY their own orders. Every endpoint that fetches an order by its identifier MUST verify ownership with is_owner_or_admin(current_user, order.user_id) before returning data.

findings.suggested_fix: After fetching the orders, filter results to those the requester is allowed to see: for each order, only include it if is_owner_or_admin(g.current_user, order.user_id) is True (or, if the endpoint is intended to be manager/admin-only for all orders, document it in api-spec.md and confirm the manager role is the intended access level). As written, a manager can read any user's order status, violating the ownership rule in security-policy.md §3.
